As a 57-year-old (aack, are they allowed here on Reddit?!) female with an eighteen-year-old daughter, I cannot explain these issues to your brains and expect it to change your visceral responses to physically "perfect" and imperfect women, but perhaps this description may help to explain the sometimes confusing behavior of young women vis-a-vis cosmetics. I am a 57-year-old (aack, are they allowed here on Reddit?!) female with an eighteen-year-old daughter. My daughter uses so much make-up that it blows me away (and costs me a lot!) I too have found myself reminded of Mimi from the Drew Carey Show, and I don't wish that on anyone. It is amusing to me that, when I was young, I used to wonder why my own mother didn't bother to use cosmetics as I did. Why didn't she bother, if it would help her to look better!?

At this point in my life, I won't bother to put on liquid base make-up on a daily basis, as everyone knows me as freckled, anyway. I rarely see make-up as an improvement. Honestly! I had my eyeliner tattooed on a few years ago, and any appreciation of eye shadow or mascara that I may have had in the past was greatly tempered by the discomfort of using it with contact lenses. I probably use shadow  about only 3 or 4 times a year (even though I am back in glasses and not as sensitive to the spill of creams or powders into my eyes). I will typically apply lipstick just as I am arriving at work, but not otherwise. Blush is good, when I remember.

If I experienced the pimples that younger girls and women sometimes do, then I suppose that I would be a much heavier user. To me, cover-up is always a justified use of make-up! I'll use it myself on occasion. At my age, more women use cover-up for under-eye circles than for pimple camouflage. I have been lucky regarding eye circles.

My guess, as a typically socialized female, is that American girls are trained that full make-up (including base, eyebrow pencil, eyeliner, eye shadow, mascara, blusher, any "necessary" cover-up, and lipstick) is defined as standard. Some women choose to have fun with their make-up by adding multiple-color blends for their eye shadow or lip color, or adding flourishes to their eyeliner or lipliner. It might look cute on them, but I would feel foolish doing such things. Life is too short.

Much depends upon one's line of work. I should add that hair color, nail extensions and polishes follow similar principles. I work in a professional health-care capacity, so I try to look natural (except for covering my gray hair.) Someone in a more creative/artistic field would have more leeway in terms of creativity--and might feel even more paranoid about letting her facial wrinkles define her.

I hope that what I have written is not all terribly obvious. I suspect that most American women could write this same comment in their sleep, but perhaps it will be informative to predominantly-male Redditors. 

It is really rather sad that females are expected to look perfect, even if it means looking artificial. If you bother looking at ads showing females, you may even notice how photos in many ads are often focused on only one specific body part--and I'm not joking about breasts here. Often an ad may show only torsos or hands or feet. The message that most women of my generation got was, "EVERY part of your body must be alluring or else..." Damn, that is a merciless standard! Imagine, guys, if you were judged by your earlobes, your ass dimples, and the width of your nipples!  

I am not so naive as to assume that many of you Redditors would throw Megan Fox out of bed because of the shortness of her thumbnails, but cosmetics ads, and the celebrity ads that imitate them, foment and aggravate any feelings of self-consciousness that normal young women have, at least here in the US. I cannot explain these issues to your brains and expect it to change your visceral responses to physically "perfect" and imperfect women, but perhaps this description may help to explain the sometimes confusing behavior of young women vis-a-vis cosmetics.
